rules.mechanism: Biological N2 fixation by Bradyrhizobium leaves readily mineralizable residue with low C:N ratio (25:1).
High C:N corn stover immobilizes soil nitrogen during early spring; persistent residue harbors fungal pathogens and rootworm egg banks.
Deep fibrous rye roots scavenge residual soil nitrates before spring rains leach them into tile drains; dense spring mulch suppresses waterhemp and marestail.

rules.warning: Terminate cereal rye at least 10-14 days prior to planting corn to prevent soil moisture depletion and nitrogen immobilization.

rules.management_rule: Do not plant soybean consecutively. Rotating to corn, wheat, or non-host forages reduces egg population density by 30-50% per year.

rules.mechanism: Extensive perennial root channels improve deep water infiltration (NASA SMAP rootzone infiltration) and provide 1st-year corn with 100-150 kg N/ha.
